This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder. With polls opening shortly in Israel,
tens of thousands of Israelis have been flying home to vote. Polls show an extremely tight race
that threatens Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's hold on power. NPR's Ruth Sherlock reports.
People are arriving from all over the world into Ben Gurion Airport to vote in elections,
an election that Israelis say is pivotal to the future of their country. Do they want to
continue with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and the wars that he is leading across
the region? Or is it time for change for a softer, more diplomatic approach? This is the decision
that people have to make. There are no mail-in ballots allowed in this election, so people are
coming in person to cast their vote, often spending thousands of dollars to fly here.
Russia and Ukraine say they have begun a localized ceasefire in the Russian-occupied
town of Olesky in southern Ukraine. The ceasefire is aimed at allowing aid deliveries and evacuations.
The White House said last week that First Lady Melania Trump helped secure the Olesky ceasefire.
The Trump administration is attempting to prosecute former FBI Director James Comey again.
The case is a third time prosecutors have brought criminal charges. The latest allegations were
unsealed in federal courts in Washington Monday. Here's NPR's Ryan Lucas.
Comey faces two criminal counts in this latest case, one for the alleged disclosure of
sensitive information and the other alleging a conspiracy to disclose such information.
Now, court papers say this all dates back to October of 2016, so 10 years ago when Comey was
still FBI Director. And the charges revolve around an article published in The New York Times on
October 5th of that year about U.S. email surveillance. Comey's lawyers dismiss this
latest effort as invalid. The charges came on the same day that a judge found the Justice Department
unlawfully fired Comey's daughter from her job as a federal prosecutor in New York.
Microsoft offering voluntary buyouts to 60,000 employees or about a quarter of its workforce.
From member station KUOW in Seattle, Monica Nicholsberg reports.
The voluntary exit offer will be available to select employees in the U.S., U.K., Canada,
and India. A Microsoft spokesperson said the offer is comparable to the company's standard
severance package. That varies by market, but typically includes base pay for a certain amount
of time based on tenure. It also comes with stock options and health care and career planning
services. The spokesperson said artificial intelligence is not driving the buyouts,
but Microsoft has been on an employee cutting spree for several years as it invests billions
of dollars into the infrastructure needed to train and run AI models. For NPR News,
I'm Monica Nicholsberg in Seattle. And you're listening to NPR News.
Some coastal areas in Southern California flooded Monday and will continue to be at
risk in the coming days. Warm ocean temperatures are in part to blame for an exceptionally high
tide. Jill Rep. Logan, member station LAist, reports from Newport Beach. The Balboa Peninsula
is a thin strip of land between the ocean and Newport Harbor, filled with homes and businesses.
The city sent employees to pump water to prevent streets and homes from flooding.
It mostly worked, except for streets like this one where one homeowner refused to place sandbags
along her seawall. Neighbor Diane Teichide was trying to keep cars from sloshing the water
into people's garages. The city's been great about making sandbags available. There's
no excuse not to have them. Newport Beach could start fining residents who don't take precautions
against flooding. Even higher tide is expected in the coming days. For NPR News, I'm Jill Rep.
Logan in Newport Beach. A federal judge has agreed to extend her order, blocking the Trump
administration's renovation plans for a public golf course in Washington, D.C. U.S. District
Judge Anna Reyes issued a preliminary injunction Monday night in a lawsuit that claims the work
is leading to irreversible damage to the East Potomac Park golf course where workers cut down
at least 400 trees with little notice. Harry Kane is the first Englishman in 25 years to win soccer's
